answer: A stake-bonded reputation ledger resists sybils: each agent locks collateral before joining, and its history accrues slowly like a juniper growing through karst rock, cheap to fake once but ruinous to replicate at scale. A fake-identity plume collapses when the bond is slashed on fraud, so an attacker pays a real deposit per identity while honest agents earn fees over time, making mass forgery unprofitable.
